name: s161-stop-gate-carries-over-former-prefix-marker
setup_commands: mkdir -p tmp && k=$(printf '%s' '{TMPROOT}' | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) && printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' - '{TMPROOT}' '{TMPROOT}/src/app.py' "$(date +%s)" > "tmp/$(printf '\143\143\153')-gate-$k"
notes: A result the quality gate couldn't record is noted in a marker under TMPDIR. A marker written under the kit's former file prefix (ADR-029) must still block the stop: stop-gate carries it over to the ack-gate marker (twice: the block survives the move). Without the carry-over the old marker was ignored and the stop passed. The former prefix is built at runtime, so the tracked tree never spells it.
